evidence_summary: The focal paper examines whether identifying as a religious person is associated with cooperative (altruistic) internationalism, operationalized as an index of support for economic aid to poorer countries and support for the United Nations, among 56,129 World Values Survey respondents in 51 countries across survey waves from 1994 to 2009. Table 4, Model 1 adjusts for religious faith and religious-service attendance, respondent political, attitudinal, and demographic variables, country-level variables, and time effects. The supplied claim describes this association and adjustment; it does not provide a causal identification strategy or results estimate.
